s1.quote: Director’s Bay … The drop-off is located close to the shoreline at a depth of 6 metres, from where the reef immediately drops steeply to a depth of 45 metres … yellow pencil coral and giant anemones

s2.quote: Directors Bay … you can dive to 40 metres here … a lot of coral and sponges on the fencing in the bay that was placed there to keep sharks away

s3.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s3.quote: Perfectly suited for divers and snorkelers. This dive site landmark is an old decaying shark fence now covered in corals and sponges

highlights.text: Old shark fence covered in coral and sponges
Yellow pencil coral and giant anemones at the drop-off

summary.text: Former Shell directors' beach on Curaçao's south coast. A narrow sandy shelf ends at a drop-off about 6 m down, then the reef falls steeply to roughly 40-45 m. The sponge- and coral-covered old shark fence is the landmark.

s1.quote: Boca Sami … Just enter the water from our dive school. After a little swim, you will find the drop-off that starts at about 6 meters and goes down to about 45 meters … sea turtles, eagle Ray’s, mini squids

highlights.text: Sea turtles, eagle rays and mini squids

s1.quote: Marie Pampoen … The dive site itself starts after exiting the bay, where you will quickly reach the drop-off … porcupinefish dancing around each other, tarpons checking you out from a distance and moray eels

highlights.text: Porcupinefish, tarpon and moray eels around the car pile

s1.quote: Cas Abou … You can enter the water right in front of the dive shop … a standard wall dive with a drop off that starts at about 6 meters … barracudas, sea cucumbers, and eagle rays

s2.quote: Cas Abou … you can simply walk from the beach into the water and don’t need to climb anything or use a boat to get there

s3.quote: Cas Abou … It’s great for beginners because you can walk into the water from the beach … The entrance fee is 10 Nafl ($6) Mon-Sat

access.value: Beach entrance fee (about 10 Nafl, higher on Sundays)

highlights.text: Mushroom-like coral formations, barracuda and eagle rays

summary.text: Walk-in shore dive from a pretty beach on the west coast: a sandy start leads to a drop-off around 6 m and a coral-covered wall. Easy navigation makes it a good beginner site.

s1.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s1.quote: Double Reef West of Santa Ana Bay, this double reef has its shallows covered with small brain corals and loads of sun anemones

s2.quote: Double Reef … Here you can find two reefs (hence the name) in the middle a big sandy area … you’d need diving shoes as there is a rocky beach

s3.quote: Double Reef … The reef consists of fan coral, yellow pencil coral and many small, round brain coral formations

highlights.text: Brain corals and sun anemones in the shallows
Two reefs separated by a wide sandy area

hazards.text: Rocky entry and surf; dive shoes needed

summary.text: Two parallel reefs separated by a big sandy area, west of Santa Ana Bay. Shallows carry small brain corals and sun anemones, with fan and pencil coral beyond. Entry over a rocky beach with some surf.

s1.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s1.quote: Superior Producer … This cargo freighter sunk in December of 1977 and is now sitting upright at a depth of 100ft/30m

s2.quote: Superior Producer … currents that can be very strong makes this dive site a good place for the advanced divers … The depth of the sand floor here is 34 metres … on the superstructure is 17 metres

s3.quote: Divers can only reach the Superior Producer when no cruise ships are in port

s4.quote: Superior Producer … without experience you can explore the wheelhouse and the cargo space

highlights.text: Upright cargo freighter; wheelhouse and holds to explore

hazards.text: No diving when a cruise ship is in port

summary.text: Cargo freighter sunk in 1977 that sits upright near the Willemstad main pier, from about 17 m on the superstructure to 34 m on the sand. Strong currents make it an advanced dive, and it is closed whenever a cruise ship is in port.

s1.quote: Snake bay … The drop-off begins at about 9 meters and descends to about 40 meters … the steep slope to the bay can be very slippery … the large number of morays and eels

s2.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s2.quote: Snake Bay … Huge Jacks chasing bait balls, Caribbean Chromies, Creole Wrasses, Southern Rays, and Turtles

highlights.text: Many moray eels
Jacks chasing bait balls, creole wrasse, rays, turtles

hazards.text: Steep, slippery slope at the entry by the pier

summary.text: Busy reef off a small pier on the west coast where the drop-off starts around 9 m and falls to about 40 m. Known for moray eels and heavy fish traffic including jacks, rays and turtles.

s1.quote: Marie Pampoen … The carpile starts around 15 meters of depth and drops down to well below 40 meters, making this a perfect spot for your deep and/or Tec dive … many invasive lionfish are hiding between the metal scrap

s2.quote: Car Pile … This artificial reef, created from a collection of sunken cars, construction equipment, and other large debris

highlights.text: Lionfish hiding in the metal scrap

summary.text: Artificial reef of sunken cars, beams and a small barge off Marie Pampoen. The debris starts around 15 m and keeps dropping well below 40 m, so it is a deep or technical dive.

s1.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s1.quote: Blue Bay Gardens A true underwater garden. Box crabs in the sand, octopus, and baby clusters of brain and star corals

s2.quote: The Garden & The Wall … Step straight into the beach at Blue Bay Beach … The Garden (left side): This vibrant coral slope begins at just 5 meters (15 feet) and gently drops to about 50 meters (165 feet)

highlights.text: Box crabs, octopus and baby brain and star corals
Gorgonians and cleaning stations on the slope

summary.text: Shore dive from Blue Bay Beach over a coral slope that begins at about 5 m and drops gently to roughly 50 m. Known for small critters such as box crabs and octopus, plus cleaning stations.

s1.quote: Step straight into the beach at Blue Bay Beach … The Wall (right side): A dramatic drop-off starting at 3 meters (10 feet) and plunging to 55 meters (180 feet) … Famous for its colorful fan corals and elkhorn corals

s2.quote: Dive Site: Blue Bay, Curacao … This is a big wall dive … quite easy to accidentally go deeper than you anticipated

highlights.text: Fan corals and elkhorn coral

hazards.text: Easy to drift deeper than planned on the wall

summary.text: Wall dive reached straight from Blue Bay Beach: the drop-off starts around 3 m and plunges past 50 m. Fan and elkhorn corals make it popular, but clear water makes it easy to go deeper than planned.

s1.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s1.quote: Shipwreck Point … This is like diving inside an aquarium! Next to our dive shop, sits one of the healthiest reefs around Curacao

s2.quote: facilitates many excellent short-trip boat dives like Car Piles, Cornelius Bay, Shipwreck Point, Saba Wreck, and Stella Maris Reef

highlights.text: One of the healthiest reefs around Curaçao, aquarium-like fish life

summary.text: Short boat dive off the Mambo Beach area on a reef described as one of the healthiest around Curaçao, with fish life like an aquarium.

s1.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s1.quote: Saba The small tugboat that sits in the shallows is called Saba, and its only at 5 meters/15 ft

s2.quote: The Saba wreck is a sunken tugboat surrounded by abundant sea life … short-trip boat dives like Car Piles, Cornelius Bay, Shipwreck Point, Saba Wreck

highlights.text: Small sunken tugboat with abundant sea life

summary.text: Small sunken tugboat lying in the shallows at only about 5 m, reached by a short boat ride from Mambo Beach. Less visited than the Tugboat Wreck and ringed by plenty of fish.

s1.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s1.quote: Barracuda Point A favorite Curacao dive, covered in dense coral formations, gorgonians and boulder corals. Turtles are spotted often on this dive site, as well as jacks and barracudas

highlights.text: Dense coral formations, gorgonians and boulder corals
Turtles, jacks and barracuda

s1.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s1.quote: Beacon Point Currents make this site an intermediate to advanced dive. You will see the largest pillar coral formation in the Caribbean at this dive

s2.quote: Beacon Point … a stunning drop-off … barracudas, groupers, nurse sharks and big Jacks … Keep the sometimes strong current in mind when you visit this boat diving site … Level: Experienced divers

highlights.text: Largest pillar coral formation in the Caribbean
Drop-off with barracuda, groupers, nurse sharks and jacks

summary.text: Boat dive on Curaçao's south coast with a stunning drop-off, big pillar coral and predators such as barracuda and nurse sharks. Current can be strong, so it suits experienced divers.

s1.publisher: Bluewater Dive Travel (Scuba Lodge & Ocean Suites)
s1.quote: Cornelius Bay Elkhorn Coral can be spotted during this dive on the plateau. Seahorses are found around the many gorgonians along the wall

s2.quote: short-trip boat dives like Car Piles, Cornelius Bay, Shipwreck Point

highlights.text: Elkhorn coral on the plateau
Seahorses among gorgonians along the wall

summary.text: Short boat dive from Mambo Beach: a coral plateau with elkhorn coral that leads to a wall draped in gorgonians, where seahorses can be found.

s1.quote: Oswaldo’s Drop Off … The drop off is only 100 yards from shore with the reef wall starting in 30 feet of water, gradually plunging to a depth of 130 feet … great snorkeling on a shallow terrace

highlights.text: Shallow terrace good for snorkeling

sites.name: Habitat

s1.quote: Rif St. Marie Habitat … The reef starts just after the beach and drops to 40 meters … a second reef edge begins at a depth of 60 meters

sites.depthNote: A second reef edge begins at about 60 m further out

s1.quote: Daaibooi Beach … vibrant coral reefs that begin just off the shore … easy water access and calm conditions … Daaibooi is known for its turtles, parrotfish, and occasionally even stingrays

highlights.text: Turtles, parrotfish and occasional stingrays

s1.quote: The Stella Maris: This is the house reef of LionsDive Beach Resort and Ocean Encounters Diving … the coral nurseries located at this site

s2.quote: the Stella Maris house reef sits inside the Curacao Marine Park … Certified divers can walk in

access.value: House reef inside the Curaçao Marine Park (LionsDive / Ocean Encounters)

highlights.text: Coral restoration nurseries on the shallow reef

summary.text: Fringing reef right off the LionsDive resort beach, inside the Curaçao Marine Park, so divers can simply walk in. Coral-restoration nurseries are rebuilding the shallow reef.
